Apple has updated its vintage and obsolete products list today, with the iPhone X and the 15-inch 2018 MacBook Pro now being listed as obsolete products. Here is an explanation of this classification.

The iPhone X and the 15-inch 2018 MacBook Pro are now listed as obsolete products

Apple today updated a support article titled "How to get repair service for out-of-warranty Apple products," moving the 15-inch 2018 MacBook Pro and the iPhone X from the vintage products list to the obsolete products list.

Apple explains that once a product is added to the obsolete list, the company will stop providing all hardware repair services, and service providers will no longer be able to order parts for it.

Products are typically classified as obsolete more than seven years after Apple stops selling them, but the actual classification time is ultimately determined by Apple.

As for Apple's vintage products list, products on it will only continue to receive repairs from Apple if parts are still in stock. Apple defines products that have been discontinued for more than five years but less than seven years as "vintage".

Apple stopped providing major operating system support for the iPhone X starting with iOS 17, with the last major version being iOS 16. The device can now only be upgraded to iOS 16.7.16 at most. As for the 15-inch 2018 MacBook Pro, it only supports up to macOS Sequoia, and the latest version installable on this model is macOS 15.7.7.

To learn more about Apple's complete vintage and obsolete products list, and under what circumstances repair service can be extended for up to 10 years, you can click this link for more details.
